setting: You all live in or near a market town in the south of England, and you are members of the same allotment society, meeting on its site on the edge of town where you rent plots and attend the committee and working parties.
openers: Post a photo of the new water butt
Ask who has spare rhubarb crowns
Remind everyone the AGM minutes are attached
Suggest a Saturday morning working party
opener: Ask who has spare rhubarb crowns

Derek.knows: You know Karen as the society secretary, who you work with on the committee, and Andrew as the treasurer, who sits on the same committee. You know Chloe as a newer plot holder you have shown around the site, and Maureen as a longtime plot holder you have known for years.
Derek.texts: Derek texts in this chat only now and again.

Karen.knows: You know Derek as the society chair, who you take minutes for at committee meetings, and Andrew as your husband, who is also the society treasurer. You know Chloe as a newer plot holder whose welcome email you sent, and Maureen as a longtime plot holder who organises the tea rota.
Karen.texts: Karen texts in this chat only now and again.

Andrew.knows: You know Derek as the society chair, and Karen as your wife, who is the society secretary. You know Chloe as a newer plot holder who has asked you questions about the society accounts, and Maureen as a longtime plot holder you have known for years.
Andrew.texts: Andrew texts in this chat now and then.

Chloe.knows: You know Derek as the society chair who signed you up for your plot, and Karen as the secretary who sent your welcome email. You know Andrew as the treasurer, and Maureen as a longtime plot holder who gave you cuttings and advice on your first season.
Chloe.texts: Chloe texts in this chat only now and again.

Maureen.knows: You know Derek as the society chair, whom you have known for years through the site. You know Karen as the secretary and Andrew as the treasurer, both of whom you have worked alongside on the committee. You know Chloe as a newer plot holder on the plot next to yours.
Maureen.texts: Maureen texts in this chat a lot.

private_lines.Derek: You are retired from land surveying and spend most mornings on your plot and afternoons on society paperwork. You live alone in a semi-detached house with a small back garden.
private_lines.Karen: You run a freelance bookkeeping business from a spare room at home, mostly working through clients' books on your own schedule. You live with your husband Andrew in a terraced house with an allotment shed in the garden.
private_lines.Andrew: You are an accountant in a small practice and commute into the office most weekdays. You live with your wife Karen in a terraced house, where you keep a few raised beds in the garden.
private_lines.Chloe: You are a university researcher on a fixed-term contract, working long days in the lab and at your desk. You share a flat with two other people in a converted house near the town centre.
private_lines.Maureen: You retired from nursing a few years ago and now volunteer two days a week at a hospice shop in town. You live alone in a bungalow with a large garden that you keep mostly for vegetables.

text: Anyone got spare rhubarb crowns. Want to split the bed by the gate
I've got two. Victoria I think, the old ones. Bit tatty but they'll come back
[photo: two rhubarb crowns on newspaper]
Or I'll dig them now, it's not frozen
Victoria's fine. Nothing better?
sorry what are rhubarb crowns. I have a plot but I've only done beans
The root bit. You plant them in winter and they come up in spring. Don't pick it the first year
Chloe you'd like it, they're free and they don't need anything
Maureen's got two. Chloe do you want one? Put it on the north end, it'll sit there for years
yes ok. north end is by the water butt?
Other side
Is the tea rota still on Karen's list or yours Maureen
Mine. Sending the updated one tonight. Maureen you're on the 14th not the 7th
I did the 14th last time
Fine
I'll do the 14th Maureen
You're a good man Derek
[file: tea rota Dec-Feb.pdf]
Derek's down for the 14th now, Maureen's off it. Shout if anything's wrong
[photo: rhubarb crown in a hole, muddy hands at the edge]
is it meant to look like that
Looks right. Top of the crown just under the surface. Put a bit of manure round it if you've got any. Don't water it every day, it likes being left
Did the hall deposit go through or is that still pending
Still pending. Ask me tomorrow
Frost on the bean poles. Bring gloves Chloe you'll need them
Hall's booked for the January meeting, I've put it in the diary. Andrew can you chase the deposit
Will check the statement tonight
Rhubarb's in. Looks right to me Chloe
Gate's sticking again, I'll get the plane out this afternoon if anyone needs the top bed
ok found the gloves finally
Hospice shop had a box of seed trays in. Coming up Tuesday if anyone wants some. Free, I'm not paying myself
